content.text: : I am not seeing the N-triples `Accept` header in your pull-request. Am I missing it? or is that a follow-on pull-request?

, I had some trouble getting the application/n-triples request to work quite right (I couldn't confirm that Jena was able to start parsing the stream immediately), so I decided to leave that for later, if it is still a desired feature.
: interesting. I wonder if the fcrepo-client needs a look. Anyways, thanks for the background. We can probably punt until a user wants the feature.
, I can't say that it wasn't working, I just wasn't sure how to check.

During the export process, the exporter attempts to automatically determine the repository root by traversing the path hierarchy of the given endpoint URL and checking each resource for the presence of a <> rdf:type fedora:RepositoryRoot triple. In cases where there is a container with many children, the request for the container can time out before the response can be generated (in our case at UMD, we have a 10 minute request timeout on our Apache frontend).
Allowing the user to explicitly specify the repository root, and thus skip the automatic detection process.
If automatic detection is still required, request the container representations as N-Triples, so the response begins streaming immediately.

renderedFields.description:
During the export process, the exporter attempts to automatically determine the repository root by traversing the path hierarchy of the given endpoint URL and checking each resource for the presence of a <> rdf:type fedora:RepositoryRoot triple. In cases where there is a container with many children, the request for the container can time out before the response can be generated (in our case at UMD, we have a 10 minute request timeout on our Apache frontend).

Solutions would include:

  • Allowing the user to explicitly specify the repository root, and thus skip the automatic detection process.
  • If automatic detection is still required, request the container representations as N-Triples, so the response begins streaming immediately.
